open_questions.question: The Overview section requires a stated priority criterion for the plan. No source establishes one. What should drive grouping order — risk reduction, implementation effort, value to active workflows, or something else?

FEAT-004 (structural/graph memory) explicitly self-declares as 'not an active work item' and FEAT-20260730150718-3e (window-only prompt variant) is marked contingent-only and deferred. Should both be formally dropped in the Fit Check, or kept as named backlog items with no sequencing slot?

Beyond the two self-flagged candidates (FEAT-004, FEAT-3e), are there other features among the 26 that no longer fit the tool's stated intent of flat/minimal-abstraction autonomous memory, and should be flagged for dropping rather than planned?

FEAT-20260805151847-eb (constrained decoding for JSON-schema-valid Haiku output) is explicitly conditioned on 'if/when nexus's extraction model is served locally' — currently it uses the Anthropic API. Should it be grouped under Local Inference Infra as a prerequisite to FEAT-2a, moved to Long-term/Exploratory, or dropped?

FEAT-20260805151847-56 (per-skill memory scope) references FEAT-006 as a dependency but FEAT-006 was not supplied as a source and is not among the 26 planned features. What is FEAT-006 and does FEAT-56's planning depend on its completion?

FEAT-20260805151847-3d (hash-based skip of unchanged memories on re-embedding) and FEAT-20260805151847-77 (reduced-dimension embeddings) are tagged 'performance/embeddings' with no declared bucket. Should they land in Retrieval & Recall (they affect recall latency) or Local Inference Infra (they affect the embedding stack)?

FEAT-20260805151847-7e (cosine-similarity zero-shot classification as a cheaper alternative to Haiku calls) is tagged 'governance, cost' but its mechanism is embedding-based. Should it be grouped under Memory Lifecycle & Governance or Local Inference Infra?

At least 12 of the 26 features are tagged 'needs-research: implementation approach not yet decided' (FEAT-2d, FEAT-cf, FEAT-56, FEAT-5a, FEAT-68, FEAT-77, FEAT-7e, FEAT-bd, FEAT-ce, FEAT-d1, FEAT-eb, FEAT-2a). Should the implementation plan include research spikes as discrete sequenced steps within each bucket, or should all 'needs-research' features be listed separately as pre-implementation investigations outside the main sequencing?

No source establishes cross-bucket sequencing priority. What constraint should determine which bucket is implemented first — for example, unblocking the most other work, highest confidence-to-effort ratio, or addressing known data-safety gaps first?

inconsistencies.description: FEAT-20260802190757-2d states 'ADR-015 disabled reflector.ts's call to vcc.compactFileInPlace()' as the decision that blocked re-enabling compaction. However, architecture.md shows ADR-015 (the 15th entry, file adr-20260730134500-2c) is titled 'Supersede-insert reference-upgrade exception in reflect() dedup' — a completely different decision. No ADR in the architecture index matches the compactFileInPlace disable. Either the feature file cites the wrong ADR number, or the relevant ADR was never recorded.
